Note::debug¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

std::string Note::debug(std::int64_t max_items = 12) const

Build A Bounded Diagnostic Description¶

debug() returns one owning string that identifies the Note’s state, geometry, dtype, and a bounded prefix of its values. It is intended for logs, assertions, debuggers, and failure messages where printing an entire large Note would hide the useful context. Unlike operator<<, it does not emit to a stream, and unlike pack(), its human-readable result is not a persistence format and must not be parsed back into a Note.

max_items is the maximum number of flat, row-major lanes included. The default is 12. If fewer lanes are shown than the Note contains, ... marks the omission. Zero deliberately shows no lanes, and negative values are clamped to zero; both therefore produce values=[...] for a non-empty Note. The limit counts lanes rather than bytes, so a displayed text cell may itself be long.

The prefix follows flat storage order regardless of rank. Shape and dtype are always reported, so truncation cannot make a matrix look like a vector or an Int64 Note look textual. Text lanes escape quotes, backslashes, and control characters while retaining valid non-ASCII text. Bytes lanes additionally escape non-ASCII octets as \xHH, preventing arbitrary binary data from being written directly into a terminal or log.

An undefined handle has the stable description Note(undefined). This makes debug() safe before defined() checks, unlike dtype and element accessors. The method does not mutate the Note. It allocates the returned string and examines at most max_items lanes, although the cost of rendering those lanes also depends on their byte lengths.

Example 1: Default And Explicit Truncation¶

const auto words = pluss::note::make({"alpha", "line\n\"q\"", "omega"});
std::cout << words.debug(2) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8, values=["alpha", "line\n\"q\"", ...])

The newline and quotes belong to the second lane; escaping keeps the diagnostic on one physical line.

Example 2: Native Dtypes Keep Their Identity¶

std::cout
    << pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{-2, 0, 7}).debug() << '\n'
    << pluss::note::make(std::vector<bool>{true, false}).debug() << '\n'
    << pluss::note::make(std::vector<double>{-0.0, 1.25}).debug() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, dtype=Int64, values=[-2, 0, 7])
Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, dtype=Bool, values=[true, false])
Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, dtype=Float64, values=[-0, 1.25])

Values are formatted from typed storage; they are not converted into Text lanes first. The sign of floating-point zero remains visible.

Example 3: Suppress All Values Without Losing Metadata¶

const auto value = pluss::note::make({"a", "b", "c"});
std::cout << value.debug(0) << '\n'
          << value.debug(-3) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8, values=[...])
Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8, values=[...])

This call form is useful when a log should disclose structure but not contents.

Example 4: Binary Lanes Are Log-Safe¶

const std::string raw{"A\0\xFF", 3};
std::cout << pluss::note::bytes(std::vector<std::string>{raw}).debug() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=bytes, values=["A\x00\xFF"])

Example 5: Undefined Is Directly Inspectable¶

std::cout << pluss::Note::undefined().debug() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(undefined)
